newsitem.title: GREECE: Upbeat banks lift Greek shares in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Upbeat banks lift Greek shares in thin trade.

text.p: Greek equities raced ahead by 1.82 percent on Wednesday, boosted by banks which rebounded from Tuesday's weakness.
Fund managers said equities were not moving in a broadly-based trend but were swayed by day-to-day oscillations of blue chip banks and industrials.

"Current trading patterns are not part of a broader market move but reflect daily performance of large cap banks and industrials which have a large effect on the benchmark index," said Dimitrios Katsabekis, a mutual fund manager at Agricultural Bank.
"This also confuses technical analysis, which remains undecided about the market's medium- to long-term potential," he added.
Low turnover was seen by fund managers as an impediment to a major swing in prices from a trading range above 1,500 points.
"Equities are at a critical point, oscillating in a trading range and base-building above 1,500 points," said Katsabekis.
"But any upward break-out will not be sustained unless turnover picks up considerably from current poor levels," he added.
The Athens general index added 1.82 percent or 28.15 points to the day's high of 1,576.33 from Tuesday' 1,548.18 close.
Turnover was moderate at 10.8 billion drachmas on volume of 2.7 million shares.
Banks led the market higher with a 2.81 percent jump, followed by construction and industrials which advanced 1.52 and 1.42 percent, respectively.
Advancing stocks led decliners 116 to 61 with 26 shares unchanged on 203 traded.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $74.90-$77.73. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,566-3,789 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $12.37-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 233-265 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
